core_concepts.concept: The per-session learning **artifact** (a captured lesson: prose + JSON record)
The **light**, per-user, single-session in-conversation capture flow that produces a learning; available in every session mode
core_concepts.bindings: `claude/guides/learning-flow.md` (guide_id `learning-flow`), `learn/collect-learning.py`, the `## Session Learning` instruction rule, private `learnings/<host>/events.jsonl` capture, `compose/instructions_store.py` selection and activated-session snapshots; user-global instruction files are preserved. Identifiers stay on the `learn`/`learning` root — the hyphen token `session-learning` is the deprecated heavy-subsystem alias (below), so it must NOT appear in light-flow identifiers

core_concepts.concept: The **heavy** curator/power-user pipeline that mines many sessions and distills them into reusable instruction items; runs only in its dedicated preset
core_concepts.bindings: `design/session-distill/` (HANDOFF, PLACEMENT-FRAMEWORK, ledger.json, versions.json), `session-distill/`, `claude/guides/session-distill-workflow.md` (+ codex/ + ko/ mirrors, `guide_id: session-distill-workflow`), `compose/domains.json` guides key, `[presets.session-distill]` + `[session_distill]` in `launch/agent-launch.toml`, `mode = "distill"`, `session-distill-state.json`, launcher `DISTILL_MODE`/`DISTILL_PRESET`/`distill_hub`/`session_distill_nudge`

core_concepts.concept: The chronological record of **decisions about developing this repo** — what was decided here and which alternative it closed. Author-side: it never ships, which is exactly what separates it from **session distill** (a feature of the deployed package, run by its users). `gates/check-package.sh` declares `decisions/` author-side and fails if it enters `files[]`. Merging it into distill later stays open

Rules, guides, and procedures that govern how a worker performs a task. The private catalog and personal authoring compile selected immutable snapshots; native sessions and explicit app tasks have separate delivery records
core_concepts.bindings: `agent-bios instructions`, Instructions Studio, `compose/instructions_catalog.py`, `compose/instructions_store.py`, `compose/instructions.py`, `compose/instructions_ui.py`, `compose/instructions_import.py`, `compose/instructions_app.py`, and their `launch/agent-launch.py` clients. Legacy command/module/env aliases and schema-v1 physical storage remain explicit compatibility interfaces; see `docs/instructions-compatibility.md`.

core_concepts.concept: A finite guided dialogue about why a coherent instruction bundle exists, its context, mechanisms and limits. Distinct from session learning (capture) and session distill (mining): compact entry guidance and requested pages expose pinned effective instructions as learning data; supporting guides are references, not an unbounded question queue. A meaningful user-first discovery may save a requested-only personal note and unlock a persistent UI trophy; semantic originality remains a judgment, not a provenance-check claim
core_concepts.bindings: `compose/instructions_understand.py` compact entry and `read`/`turns` paging, `claude/skills/understand/SKILL.md`, `launch/agent-launch.py` Understand! menu and `--understand`, private user `understand/state.json` reset generation

core_concepts.concept: **Deep review** — a deep check on an IMPLEMENTATION (functional, adversarial, logic, scenario, stress). **One concept, two host-bound mechanisms, both the host CLIs themselves**: `ultracode` runs on Claude (the Claude Code CLI's own dynamic workflow — many agents, each candidate finding adversarially verified — opened by the keyword in the prompt), `codex-exec` runs on Codex (the CLI's non-interactive exec mode: the whole packet handed to one frontier-effort pass). Personal or third-party reviewers are not shipped; they register in the user-owned methods file
core_concepts.bindings: `[capabilities.ultracode]` + `[review_methods.ultracode]` (Claude, the `claude` backend); `[capabilities.codex-exec]` + `[review_methods.codex-exec]` (Codex, the `codex` backend). The legacy `review_setup`/route token `"ultracode"` is a **different namespace** — a setup name, frozen — and is bound to its tool through `LEGACY_ULTRACODE_CAPABILITY` in `launch/agent-launch.py` rather than by sharing the string, which is what lets the tool be replaced without renaming the route

core_concepts.concept: The declared, per-review definition of defect for a system type × work goal — observer, defect, evidence bar, non-defects, classification enum (ONE class stop-relevant), stop condition, misclassification cost, goldens — chosen and declared BEFORE the review starts. Nearest neighbors, distinguished on purpose: the **severity ladder** answers *how bad*, never *whether* — a loop can plateau entirely inside "material"; **deep review** names mechanisms, and a criterion is what any mechanism is handed; **consumption surface** names where knowledge reaches a model. Ordering: system type + goal → defect criterion → classification → defect? → severity → materiality → stop evaluation
core_concepts.bindings: `claude/guides/review-defect-criteria.md` (+ ko/ + generated codex mirrors, `guide_id: review-defect-criteria`), `compose/domains.json` guides key; routed from `claude/guides/review-request.md` ("Declare the criterion") and the Review Loop of `claude/guides/coding-staged-workflow.md`

core_concepts.concept: A place knowledge or a tool reaches a model from — global bullet, guide, hook injection, agent description or body, launch contract, MCP tool list, personal learnings — together with the zero-context places that shape behavior without entering the window: enforcement defaults, gates, receipt adjudication, capability withholding. **Extends `capability surface`** rather than forking a second word: both name what the runtime makes available, one at call time and one at load time. The dated 2026-07-18 routing record calls its subset **layers** and orders them by cheapness; that word stays in that record and is not a live identifier
core_concepts.bindings: `SURFACES.md` — the catalog and each surface's admission bar. Realized by `compose/assemble.py` (tiering, audience filtering), the router bullets in `claude/CLAUDE.md`, `claude/hooks/`, `claude/agents/` + `codex/agents/`, `launch/agent-launch.py` (contract projection, MCP registration, receipt adjudication), `wrappers/`, `gates/`

core_concepts.concept: A **procedure for one task**, packaged as `SKILL.md` with name/description and supporting files. Selected requested procedures and the management bootstrap remain private snapshot resources; no-instructions mode emits neither. The optional explicit-use app bridge has a separate native discovery entry with implicit invocation disabled; registering it does not select instruction content
core_concepts.bindings: `claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, `compose/domains.json` skills, `compose/check-domains.py`, `compose/instructions_catalog.py`, `compose/bootstrap/SKILL.md`, `compose/instructions_store.py`, `compose/app_bridge/`, `compose/instructions_app.py`, `SURFACES.md` "Requested procedure", "Private management bootstrap" and "App discovery metadata"

core_concepts.concept: A repository's **own layer** of agent instruction — its `AGENTS.md` body and `CLAUDE.md` shim — which agent-bios **teaches how to fill and never fills**: the produced file belongs to that repository, carries no marker or version, and is never a deploy or prune target. The repo-charter skill produces it by reading invariants and traps out of the code

A question with resolver.kind=none is a declared gap, not an oversight — ontology/check-ontology.py fails if a P1 question has no working resolver. Every question names the purpose clause whose decisions it serves; a question serving none is retired, with its reason kept so the retirement is auditable rather than a silent delete.

target.clause: A corpus catalog exists and users select from it; a default-loaded corpus also exists, so deployment and loading are separate guarantees. A corpus package can be ADDED to an existing install regardless of how it was installed, and removal works both wholesale and per package — preferably by fetching the additional corpus from inside the service after install, not by re-running a different install mode.
target.licenses: foreclosure questions only — whether current work makes this impossible or expensive later; NOT questions about implementation that does not exist
open_foreclosure_questions: Today assemble.py bundles only core+infra+SELECTED domains, so nothing is deployed-but-unloaded. Does the catalog keep select-then-deploy, or move to deploy-then-select? Only the latter puts R3 under tension.

answered_foreclosure_questions.q: canary echoes ONE bundle rev marker. If catalog items load independently, does that probe still prove what loaded — and does the prune it authorizes then delete the wrong thing?
answered_foreclosure_questions.a: Nothing is foreclosed, because the rev was never the authorization. `learn/migrate-learnings.py::placed_here` is, and it asks the filesystem whether the promoted anchor is in this user's deployed corpus rather than trusting build-time audience metadata, which is per-item evidence that survives packages diverging. The rev (`corpus_loaded`) is a coarser precondition above it, and non-core packages are refused outright — `pkgid.resolve(p) != CORE` keeps, on the stated grounds that only core's composition can be confirmed today, with `foreign package -> KEEP` as a self-test control. So per-package loading cannot cause a wrong delete under current code. The requirement this leaves belongs to the stage that makes non-core packages prunable, not to today's work: presence is exactly what PU-13 says cannot prove loading, so when a foreign package becomes prunable, `placed_here` must be paired with per-package loading evidence. One global rev cannot supply that, and the failure it would allow is deployed-but-not-loaded content authorizing an unrecoverable delete.

answered_foreclosure_questions.q: Full mode writes the corpus into the entry file the user then owns and edits — how does a package get added later?
answered_foreclosure_questions.a: User edits and additions are managed as a separate version from ours. Once our content and theirs are separable, adding a package edits only our side.

answered_foreclosure_questions.q: Per-package removal needs to know which bytes came from which package, and nothing records that.
answered_foreclosure_questions.a: It does not need byte provenance. Removal is by artifact bundle — a set of versions — so install and uninstall need not be traceable to individual bytes.

answered_foreclosure_questions.q: What does uninstall owe the user's own content?
answered_foreclosure_questions.a: Uninstall is a SECURITY operation: everything of ours goes, with nothing left behind. That is only safe once the user's own content is separately versioned, which is why the first answer is a prerequisite for this one.

contradiction.claim: a span written into a user-owned file is identifiable as ours and carries matching merge/check/remove; the entry files are never manifested

sites.install.sh full mode: deploys the entry CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md through deploy_file, which manifests unconditionally; uninstall replays the manifest with rm -f
sites.install.sh packaged mode: the entry is seeded and not manifested, as the comment above assemble_packaged says
sites.compose/assemble.py: writes settings hook registrations and the AGENTS.md central region with a merge path and no remover

contradiction.no_declaration_because: nothing states that the ownership rule is packaged-mode-only, and nothing states that those two spans are exempt from the removal half.
contradiction.was: the demoted PU-14, which is why GR-12 needed a new root
contradiction.choice: Keep the rule and fix the code, with one refinement the implementation forced: full mode's entry file stays a deploy target. In that mode the entry file IS the corpus, so not manifesting it would leave the whole corpus behind after uninstall — trading data loss for junk the user cannot identify as ours. The real defect was that uninstall deleted with no backup while install backs up before overwriting. That asymmetry is closed, and the two merge-only spans now have removers.
contradiction.prevents: gates/test-assemble.sh scenario S7 — our settings registration and the AGENTS.md central region are removed, another tool's hook and the personal section survive.

contradiction.claim: the two install modes' coexistence is either a transition or the permanent design

sites.compose/canary.sh: calls the full-mode no-bundle shape 'by design'
sites.design/adapter-split/ECOSYSTEM-ARCHITECT: defers the multi-package composer without saying what happens to the full path

contradiction.no_declaration_because: the shape is declared; which of the two it is, is not. That is the half deciding who owns the loading obligation.
contradiction.choice: Transitional, with the end condition now stated. The two modes are not two permanent contracts: a full install must be able to gain a corpus package later, and removal must work both wholesale and per package. The install SHAPES may differ; what must converge is the capability. The preferred route is fetching additional corpus from inside the service after install rather than re-running a different install mode.
contradiction.prevents: PT-1 carries the requirement, so a foreclosure question is admitted against any work that would make post-install package acquisition harder.
contradiction.outcome: Closed by landing the end condition rather than by choosing a side: the modes converged the same day the decision was recorded.

decisions.note: Choices the ontology made. A5 exists because some were recorded as observations — a status asserted as though read off the code when it was a judgement between alternatives. An open decision names its alternatives so the next reader can see what was NOT chosen.

rows.claim: Three of twelve deploy targets carry no verify assertion: the two Codex wrappers and the agents directory.
rows.sites: ontology/extract.py computes the uncovered set from real deploy_file / verify_match call sites; install.sh cmd_verify asserts none of the three.
options: add verify_match for the wrappers and the agents directory, making the deployed copies byte-checked like the rest
declare the three exempt with a stated reason — a wrapper is re-deployed on every install, so drift is self-healing and byte-checking it buys little
move the wrapper deploy onto the assembler path, where coverage already exists, so the question stops existing
rows.consequence: GR-4's status, and whether `verify` claims more coverage than it has.
rows.retro_note: The graph carried status `violated` — the judgement that this gap is a defect rather than a licensed exemption — with no record that the second reading was considered. The status was authored; it read as observed.
rows.choice: Declare the three exempt rather than add assertions.
rows.rationale: A wrapper and the agents directory are re-deployed in full on every install, so drift between source and deployed copy is self-healing on the next run and a byte assertion buys little. GR-4's status stops being `violated`; the exemption is the answer, not the absence of a check.

rows.claim: uninstall backs up what it removes and deliberately keeps the state dir
rows.sites: install.sh cmd_uninstall writes backups/uninstall-<ts> and prints 'Kept: managed venv + backups'; the same command is the one a user runs to get our content OFF the machine.
options: purge the state dir and stop backing up on uninstall — correct once the user's own content is separable, wrong before it, since full mode's entry file still mixes both
keep the backup until user content is separated, then remove it — safe but leaves a security operation incomplete in the meantime
bundle everything into one artifact outside the managed paths, then purge — chosen
rows.consequence: Whether `uninstall` means 'stop using it' or 'leave no trace'. The user says the latter.
rows.retro_note: Today's change added the uninstall backup to close a data-loss path. The security framing arrived after, and inverts it: preserving what was removed is the defect, not the fix. Both readings are right about different content, which is why the separation has to land first.
rows.choice: Neither option as posed. Everything removed leaves as ONE archive outside every managed path, and every managed location is then purged — state dir, backups, cache, venv, and the loose .bak-* copies sitting in the user's own config dirs. The archive can be collected centrally or deleted in a single act.
rows.rationale: The two constraints were only in conflict while the copy had to STAY on the machine. Moving it into one handoff artifact satisfies both at once, and it removes the ordering dependency: the purge no longer waits on separating the user's content from ours, because nothing is destroyed by it.
rows.prevents: gates/check_parity.py::uninstall_leaves_no_trace runs the real command against a throwaway HOME and asserts both halves — nothing of ours survives, and a line only the user wrote is inside the archive.
